origin.description: Choose between two series according to a test, after aligning them on the union of their indexes.

arguments.name: test
arguments.text: A zoo series, or a vector placed on the index of yes.

arguments.name: yes
arguments.text: Values used where test is true.

arguments.name: no
arguments.text: Values used where test is false. A scalar is recycled.

origin.details: ifelse is not a generic, so the call is written ifelse.zoo. The three arguments that are zoo series are aligned on the union of their indexes, with NA in the gaps. A missing test stays missing. On a series 1, NA, 3, the test greater than 1 selects 0, NA, 3.
origin.value: A zoo series with the aligned index of test.

translation.details: The zoo arguments are aligned on the union of their indexes, with missing values in the gaps. A missing test stays missing. Comparison keeps a missing observation missing, so a series 1, NA, 3 tested against 1 selects 0, NA, 3.
translation.value: A Zoo series with the aligned index of test.
translation.example:
import math
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/ahmed/killr_projects/killr/packages/zoo")
from zoo.zoo_class import aggregate_zoo, ifelse_zoo, is_zoo, median_zoo, quantile_zoo, rev_zoo, xtfrm_zoo, zoo


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, (bool, np.bool_)):
        print("TRUE" if value else "FALSE")
        return
    if is_zoo(value):
        show(value.data)
        show(value.index)
        return
    array = np.asarray(value, dtype=float).ravel(order="F")
    print(" ".join("NA" if math.isnan(float(item)) else format(float(item), ".16g") for item in array))

z = zoo([1, float('nan'), 3], [1, 2, 3])
show(ifelse_zoo(z > 1, z, 0))
